one_liner: Rust per-packet binary telemetry format (MTS-1/MWire) reporting ~5% smaller payloads than MessagePack on synthetic host metrics.
what_it_does: MTS-1 (Magenta Telemetry Specification v1) is the wire format of the author's Magenta host-monitoring agent. The paper does not link any code, but the author's Rust workspace ndourc/mwire implements the format, and its committed tele20k/tele50k datasets match the paper's Table I S2/S3 byte counts exactly for JSON, JSONL, CBOR, MessagePack and MTS-1+LZ4. It has two encodings. The legacy per-packet format serializes a fixed 17-metric `TelemetryData` struct: a 15-byte header, the device ID, a 16-byte UUID, tagged fields and a CRC32. The newer 'MTS1 stream' serializes JSON arrays as a schema table plus snapshot/delta frames, with optional whole-body LZ4. The API is `encode(&TelemetryData)` / `decode(&[u8])`, plus `encode_stream` / `decode_stream` over `HashMap<String, MtfValue>` and a `mwire` CLI; it is not a MessagePack drop-in.
how_it_is_fast: The win is in size, not speed. Each present field is a 1-byte tag (3-bit type, 5-bit field number) followed by a fixed-width little-endian value, absent fields are skipped, and the UUID is stored as 16 raw bytes. In the paper's generator this gives a constant 139 B per record: a 2 B length prefix, 15 B header, 18 B device ID, 16 B UUID, 84 B payload and 4 B CRC. The 'delta' mode is change suppression: a delta packet or frame carries the new values of fields that changed (optionally only past a per-field epsilon), not arithmetic differences. Per-packet LZ4 (lz4_flex block mode) is optional.
when_to_use: Reproducing or auditing the paper: the repo's generate_dataset binary and committed tele20k/tele50k files let you re-derive Table I byte counts.

Rust host agents sending fixed host metrics (CPU %, temperature, frequency, memory, disk, network counters, uptime) where you own both ends and want a checksummed packet with timestamp, sequence number and a LAN-proxy flag.
Slowly changing metric streams stored as JSON arrays, where the MTS1 stream mode stores field names once and writes only changed fields between snapshots (every 10th record by default).
As a small reference design for a telemetry packet layout: the core crate is about 100 KB of Rust in 7 files, with no unsafe code.
when_not_to_use: You need speed numbers. No encode or decode timings are published. The README's ~65,000 encode / ~112,000 decode records/s gives no hardware, method or baseline, and no results from the criterion comparison bench are published.

You want a fair size win over MessagePack. The 5.4% margin exists because the baseline stores the UUID as a 36-char hex string (38 B) while MTS-1 stores 16 raw bytes. By my arithmetic on the generator code (not a measurement), rmp-serde MessagePack with a binary UUID would be ~127 B per record vs MTS-1's 139 B.

C++ codebases, or platforms without prebuilt artifacts. It is Rust only, with no C/C++ API. The only prebuilt artifacts are a Windows x86-64 mwire.exe and a single PyPI wheel (magenta-telemetry 0.1.0, CPython 3.11 win_amd64). Nothing is published on crates.io.

Untrusted input. The decoders call `Vec::with_capacity` / `HashMap::with_capacity` with u32 counts read from the packet, and CRC32 is not authentication, so a crafted packet can request very large allocations.

Production dependencies. It is single-author code (5 stars, 6 commits from 2026-02-15 to 2026-03-01, no issues filed) with no root LICENSE file. The packet format has a fixed field table (numbers 0-31). A lost snapshot breaks delta reconstruction, and an epsilon above 0 makes delta mode lossy.

integration.form: crate (Cargo workspace: magenta-telemetry-core lib, mwire CLI, pyo3 and wasm-bindgen bindings); not on crates.io, so use a git/path dependency or source-drop
integration.dependencies: core: lz4_flex 0.11, crc32fast 1.4, serde 1.0, serde_json 1.0; CLI adds clap 4.5, anyhow, rmp-serde 1.3, ciborium 0.2; bindings add pyo3 0.21 or wasm-bindgen 0.2
integration.platforms: Pure Rust with no unsafe in core/src, so it should build for any Rust target; prebuilt binaries exist only for Windows x86-64
integration.thread_safety: not documented (core encode/decode are stateless free functions; delta reconstruction state is held by the caller)

gotchas: The paper's 'delta-encoded' results do not use delta mode. generate_dataset.rs calls `encode()` on full records with `is_delta` false, so Table I measures plain fixed-width packets. The constant 139 B per record is therefore the natural packet size, not evidence of computed numbers.

The paper and the code describe different methods. The paper cites real Magenta samples at ~30 s intervals and deltas of c_i - c_(i-1). The generator uses sin/cos synthetic values at 1 s intervals with one device ID and UUID, and delta frames carry replacement values. The paper's 100-host example (1.95 GB vs 0.24 GB, '87.7%') also disagrees with its own 548 B vs 139 B per payload.

The two spec documents disagree. docs/FORMAT.md's type-ID table (e.g. 0x01 = Null) and its legacy flag bits do not match core/src/types.rs and encoder.rs, which follow FORMAT_SPEC.md (0x06 = Null, delta = flag bit 4). Treat the code as the spec.

Per-packet LZ4 makes these packets larger (2,794,270 vs 2,780,000 B on S2) because `compress_prepend_size` adds a 4-byte length and the ~84-byte payload barely compresses. Only the stream mode's whole-body LZ4 pays off: DISTRIBUTION_README reports 1,340,041 vs 4,440,224 B on a 25,957-record dataset.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only if you want a ready-made, CRC-checked host-metrics packet in Rust. For compactness alone, JSON BinPack (smallest or tied-smallest across 27 documents) and qdf (IoT/OTLP batch fixtures) have broader size evidence, and fernBuffer's MessagePack comparison covers more data shapes.
verified_claims_summary: The only claim is size: on a synthetic 10k-record set, per-packet MTS-1 totals 1,390,000 B vs 1,469,521 B for MessagePack (rmp-serde, structs as arrays) and 5,475,079 B for JSON (5.4% and 74.6% smaller), and the 20k and 50k sets scale linearly. Protobuf was not measured, and no compiler, hardware or timings are given. My arithmetic on the repo's generator reproduces the MessagePack and MTS-1 byte counts exactly for all three sizes.
status_note: Single-author research code behind a non-peer-reviewed January 2026 arXiv preprint: last commit 2026-03-01, one v1.0.0 Windows release, MIT according to the README and Cargo.toml but with no root LICENSE file; use it as a reference, not a maintained dependency.
